original_question: Suppose a Banach space X has density ω_1. Does the family wk(X) of all nonempty weakly compact subsets of X have property (SC), meaning that there exists a set selector ψ on wk(X) such that ψ ∘ F is scalarly measurable for every scalarly measurable multifunction F with values in wk(X)?
target_in_paper: Section 2.3, Problem 2.8 (Fremlin): Suppose dens(X)=ω1. Does wk(X) have property (SC)?
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s actual target very closely. It has the right hypothesis (density character ω1), the right family wk(X) of nonempty weakly compact subsets of X, and the right property (SC): the existence of a universal set selector ψ whose composition with every scalarly measurable wk(X)-valued multifunction is scalarly measurable.
missing_details: The paper’s standing convention is that all Banach spaces are real.
The measurable-domain context from Section 2.3 should be made explicit: one fixes a complete probability space (Ω, Σ, μ).
A set selector on wk(X) is a map ψ:wk(X)→X satisfying ψ(K)∈K for every K∈wk(X).
A wk(X)-valued multifunction is a map F:Ω→wk(X).
Scalar measurability of a multifunction F means F^{-}(H):={t∈Ω: F(t)∩H≠∅} belongs to Σ for every open half-space H⊆X.
Scalar measurability of a function f:Ω→X means x*∘f is Σ-measurable for every x*∈X*; the paper also notes that this is equivalent to Ba(X,w)-measurability.
For full paper-faithfulness, the hypothesis should be written in the paper’s notation as dens(X)=ω1.
refined_question: Fix a complete probability space (Ω, Σ, μ), and let X be a real Banach space with dens(X)=ω1. Write wk(X) for the family of all nonempty weakly compact subsets of X. Does wk(X) have property (SC), i.e. does there exist a set selector ψ:wk(X)→X with ψ(K)∈K for every K∈wk(X) such that, for every scalarly measurable multifunction F:Ω→wk(X) in the sense that F^{-}(H):={t∈Ω: F(t)∩H≠∅}∈Σ for every open half-space H⊆X, the function ψ∘F:Ω→X is scalarly measurable (equivalently, x*∘(ψ∘F) is Σ-measurable for every x*∈X*)?
equivalent_formulation: With the same setup, does there exist a set selector ψ:wk(X)→X such that ψ∘F is Ba(X,w)-measurable for every scalarly measurable multifunction F:Ω→wk(X)?
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem 2.8 in Section 2.3, not the neighboring Problem 2.9 about convex weakly compact sets. The draft is already almost verbatim in substance, but it is not fully stand-alone because it omits the subsection’s ambient complete probability space and the formal definitions introduced immediately before Problem 2.8: multifunction, selector, scalar measurability for multifunctions and functions, set selector, property (SC), and the notation wk(X). The nearby context also explains why this is the sharp question asked in the paper: wk(X) is already known to have property (SC) when X* is w*-separable, or when (X*,w*) is angelic of density character ω1, while Fremlin proved that wk(X) can fail property (SC) in general, even for Hilbert spaces.
